subject: Re: Tier merge & feature bundle clarification — ReefCare pilot
messages:
From: Natalie Park <natalie@reefcare.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@reefcare.ai>
Date: Sat, 07 Jun 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tier merge and feature mapping question for pilot

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. We're finalizing the scope for our 3-month pilot and have a couple of packaging questions before we sign the SOW. Quick summary:

- We want to combine two pilot modules (chat + extraction) under a single reserved tier rather than separate bundles. Will that change the committed throughput calculation?
- Are there limits on enabling the "structured-output" feature across both modules under the compact tier, or is that considered an addon?
- If we start on the compact tier and need to upgrade mid-pilot to stable throughput, what's the proration approach for credits/committed units?

I've attached the ReefCare_Requested_Specs.xlsx with the expected traffic pattern. Can you confirm if the compact tier can support burst to our expected 250 req/s for short windows, or should we plan a direct upgrade to mid-tier?

Appreciate a short note + recommended path.

Best,
Natalie Park
Head of Product, ReefCare AI

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Park <natalie@reefcare.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jun 2025 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tier merge and feature mapping question for pilot

Hi Natalie — thanks for the clear summary and the traffic spreadsheet. Short answers up front:

- Combining chat + extraction under a single reserved tier is fine; we calculate committed throughput against the aggregate token/req profile. That typically reduces overhead compared to two separate bundles.
- "structured-output" counts as a feature flag, not a billable addon for pilot customers if enabled across a single reserved tier. For production licensing it can be gated as an addon per-seat, but we won't charge extra during the pilot.
- Upgrades mid-pilot are handled pro rata: you pay the delta in committed monthly cost for the remainder of the billing cycle and we credit unused hours from the prior tier. We can show a sample calc once you pick upgrade timing.

On burst: compact tier supports short bursts via our auto-burst buffer, but sustained 250 req/s for long periods will push you to mid-tier. Based on your spreadsheet, I'd recommend starting compact with a planned thumbs-up to jump to mid-tier if more than ~30% of days exceed 90th-percentile load.

I'll loop Ben on pricing/discounting options so we can include formal numbers in the SOW. Would you prefer a fixed step-up amendment (compact -> mid) or a credit-based buffer option for burst headroom?

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Park <natalie@reefcare.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Tier merge and feature mapping question for pilot

Hi Natalie — looping in Lauren for coverage on any concession asks. Appreciate the spreadsheet — looks straightforward.

Pricing options we can propose for the pilot:

1) Step-up amendment (recommended)
   - Start on Compact Reserved: baseline committed throughput 150 req/s
   - Auto-upgrade to Mid Reserved if 3-day rolling average exceeds 160 req/s
   - Proration: pay pro rata delta from upgrade time; previous tier credit applied at hourly granularity
   - No extra charge for structured-output during pilot

2) Burst-Credit buffer
   - Keep Compact Reserved baseline 150 req/s
   - Pre-purchase 200k burst credits usable toward short windows at compact latency SLA
   - Credits priced at a blended discounted rate (10% below list)
   - Unused credits expire at pilot end

3) Mid-tier pilot (flat)
   - Commit to Mid Reserved with negotiated discount; simpler but higher short-term cost

Concession note: we can offer a one-time pilot discount applied to committed spend (up to 12% off list) if ReefCare signs a 9-month pilot + selected conversion milestone into an annual contract. Any deeper discounts would need leadership approval.

Next steps: if you pick option 1 or 2 I can draft a short amendment for signature. If you want option 3 we'll show the discounted MID pricing. Also attaching a proposed amendment (Proposed_Amendment_v2.pdf) with the step-up language for review.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Natalie Park <natalie@reefcare.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Tier merge and feature mapping question for pilot

Thanks everyone — quick governance note from our side.

Ben — approved: up to 12% pilot discount is fine if we get the 9-month pilot + conversion milestone in the SOW. For the step-up amendment, please include the following guardrails in the amendment text:
- Max of two automatic step-ups during the pilot term (we'll require manual approval for subsequent steps)
- A one-time grace window (48 hours) where we will apply emergency burst capacity with no immediate charge; usage will be invoiced against the burst-credit pool post-grace window
- Structured-output remains non-billable during pilot; convert to addon only after conversion to annual contract

Natalie — if that works for ReefCare, Ben will issue the redlineable amendment and I'll sign off on the discount on execution. If you'd rather avoid a step-up, option 2 (burst credits) is also acceptable and keeps billing predictable.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Strategy, Redwood Inference
